\chapter{Learning Theory — Union Bound}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.JohnsonLindenstrauss.UnionBound
\section{Overview}

This module assembles the Johnson--Lindenstrauss lemma from single-vector
concentration by a union bound over all ordered pairs of a finite point set
$V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$.  It introduces the $(1\pm\varepsilon)$ pairwise
distortion predicate, the notion of an $\varepsilon$-JL embedding, and the
``bad pair'' event, and then extracts an embedding by the probabilistic method
whenever the union-bound failure probability is strictly below $1$.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Probabilistic method for JL embeddings]
\lean{exists_isJLEmbedding_of_pair_bound}
\label{exists_isJLEmbedding_of_pair_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BadPair, BadSingle, IsJLEmbedding, jl_union_bound}
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\Omega$, let
$A : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^{k\times d}$ be a measurable random matrix, let
$\varepsilon\in\mathbb{R}$, and let $V$ be a finite subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$.
Suppose that for every ordered pair $u, v \in V$ the bad event
$\{\omega \mid \texttt{BadSingle}\,\varepsilon\,(A\,\omega)\,(u-v)\}$ is
measurable and has probability at most $2\exp(-k\varepsilon^2/8)$, and that
the union-bound failure probability satisfies
\[
  |V|^2 \cdot 2\exp(-k\varepsilon^2/8) < 1 .
\]
Then there exists a linear map $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^k$ which is an
$\varepsilon$-JL embedding of $V$, i.e.\ $(1-\varepsilon)\|u-v\|^2 \le
\|f u - f v\|^2 \le (1+\varepsilon)\|u-v\|^2$ for all $u, v \in V$.
\end{theorem}
